title: Tenali Raman Tale 145

full_text:
An envoy from the Chola kingdom of the south arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, presenting three deep philosophical questions from his king:
'First: Who is the richest man in the world?
Second: Who is the poorest man in the world?
Third: Who is the most invincible warrior in the universe?'

The court ministers gave conventional answers:
'The richest is the Emperor with the most gold; the poorest is the beggar in rags; the most invincible is the general with the largest army!'
The Chola envoy shook his head: 'Those are common answers of common minds.'

Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, allow me to answer the Chola King’s inquiry.'

Tenali addressed the envoy:
'First: The **richest man in the world** is he who is completely content with what he has, who desires no more than what honest labor provides, and whose heart is free from envy! A contented man possesses the wealth of the universe!'

The envoy smiled: 'And who is the poorest?'
Tenali continued:
'Second: The **poorest man in the world** is the greedy king or miser who owns mountains of gold, yet tosses awake at night tormented by the craving for more! His soul is a bottomless pit of starvation, and no wealth can ever satisfy his spiritual poverty!'

The envoy nodded with deep reverence: 'And who is the most invincible warrior?'
Tenali concluded:
'Third: The **most invincible warrior in the universe** is not he who conquers ten thousand enemies with sword and lance, but he who conquers his own anger, his own pride, and his own selfish desires!
He who has conquered himself can never be defeated by any earthly foe!'

The Chola envoy was moved to tears by the sublime spiritual depth of Tenali’s answers.
He bowed low, presented Tenali with a golden medallion of honor, and declared:
'Emperor Krishnadevaraya, your empire is truly invincible, for it is guided by the wisdom of Tenali Raman!'
The King embraced Tenali, celebrating that moral truth outshines all earthly power.
moral: True royalty is defined by benevolence, true wisdom by humility, and true strength by self-mastery.
